message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for binary classification problems. It models the probability that a given input belongs to one of two classes (e.g., “yes” vs. “no”) by applying the logistic (sigmoid) function to a linear combination of the input features. The output of the logistic function is a value between 0 and 1, which can be interpreted as a probability. By setting a threshold (commonly 0.5), the model assigns each input to one of the two classes. Logistic regression is widely used because it’s simple, interpretable, and works well when the relationship between the predictors and the log‑odds of the outcome is approximately linear.
